hero.credit: This is a crop of an 1861 map created by O.N. Snow.  The entire map can be found in the Library of Congress here, and shows Virginia, Delaware, Maryland & West Virginia. Text box and circles were added by TwoScarsUp based on descriptions in the books History of the 2nd Regiment, West Virginia Cavalry Volunteers by Joseph Sutton; Lee's Endangered Left by Richard R. Duncan, and Official Reports of Averell and Confederate pursuers here.
hero.description: After the Battle of Cover Mountain in the American Civil War, Union General William W. Averell led his force to the Virginia & Tennessee Railroad. After destroying a small segment of the rail line, he began a difficult route north in rain and mountainous terrain while pursued by Confederate forces.
categories: Maps of the Battle of Cove Mountain

gallery.credit: Library of Congress Prints and Photographs Division, Brady's National Photographic Portrait Galleries  The exact same photo was published near the front of History of the Third Pennsylvania Cavalry, Sixtieth Regiment Pennsylvania Volunteers, in the American Civil War, 1861-1865., Volume 3, Part 4, which was published by the Franklin Printing Company in Philadelphia in 1905. The author is listed as United States, 3rd Pennsylvania Calvary Regiment. The cover of the book says William Brooke Rawie, and the inside says "Compiled by the Regimental History Committee in Accordance with a Resolution of the Third Pennsylvania Cavalry Association." The OCLC number is 1683643.
gallery.description: William Woods Averell (1832–1900) was a United States Army officer and a cavalry general in the American Civil War. After the war he was a diplomat and became wealthy by inventing American asphalt pavement.

gallery.source: Prelude to Battle of Cove Mountain
gallery.description: During May 1864 in the American Civil War, Union General William W. Averell tried to lure his pursuer into mountainous terrain where Averell would have an advantage. Averell's target was Wytheville, Virginia and nearby lead mines. Confederate General John H. Morgan was not fooled and took the shortest route to Wytheville, and his forces stopped Averell north of Wytheville at a mountain pass.
categories: Maps by G. W. & C. B. Colton & Co.

gallery.title: File:Battle of Cove Mountain v2.png
gallery.description: This shows the approximate positions of troops at the Battle of Cove Mountain in the American Civil War, although they moved around--especially the 34th OVMI. Positioning is based on a New York Times article from May 22, 1864; the book History of the Second Regiment, West Virginia Cavalry Volunteers; Averell's OR, and the book 13th Kentucky Cavalry, CSA: "Caudill's Army".
categories: Maps of the Battle of Cove Mountain
